name: Diamonds
description:
Diamonds

    enumi1

  1. Guest-Token — One hearth owes food, bed, and steel at dawn. `[SOCIAL]`

    The token is a knucklebone from a feast. The host's name is carved on it. Break it, and the obligation ends. The host will not thank you. There are eight notches on the bone. The ninth is the breaking.

    Blood-price: 3 cows. If you are wronged by the host, you may demand this value in cattle or public apology.

  2. Guide's Braid — Lawful passage on named sheepwalks (once). `[TRAVEL]`

    The braid is woven from horsehair and a promise. Unravel it to return. The promise was made to a hill guide who died last winter. His ghost still checks the knots. The braid has eight strands. The ninth is a memory.

    Guest-right cost: Using the braid obliges you to leave an offering at the guide's cairn (1 Supply). If you forget, start Ancestral Grudge +1.

  3. Ford Remission — Cross Wergild Ford free for a season; water as ally. `[TRAVEL]` `[WEIGHT]`

    The remission is a white stone. Skip it across the ford to pay. The stone was taken from a Viterran courthouse. The law has not found it yet. The stone has eight facets. The ninth is a crack.

    Blood-price: The stone can be used as payment for any wergild of 5 cows or less. Once used, it crumbles.

  4. Feud-Charter — Two clans sheath blades until the next harvest. `[SOCIAL]` `[OATH]`

    The charter is a broken spear. Each clan keeps a half. The spear was used to kill a Viterran tax collector. His family still wants it back. The spear had eight notches. The ninth broke it.

    Cairn vote: The charter is witnessed by the cairns. If either clan breaks it, the cairns vote for war automatically.

  5. Bloom Allotment — Claim on a week's iron from a hill bloomery. `[TRADE]`

    The bloomery is a woman's name. She decides how much you get. She is an Aeler outcast's granddaughter. Her iron is harder than any lowlander's steel. She counts her blooms in eights. The ninth is for the cairn.

    Blood-price: The iron can be traded for 2 Supply or used to forge a weapon (grant +1 die on one melee attack).

  6. Watch-Code — Today's beacon order from Three-Fires Ridge. `[WATCH]` `[TRAVEL]`

    The code is a sequence of smoke puffs. Read it, and the hills will watch for you. The code changes weekly. The fire wardens burn the old codes—the smoke carries the memory. The code has eight signals. The ninth is a warning.

    Guest-right cost: To receive the code, you must share a secret with the fire warden. If you lie, the code is false—start False Alarm [4].

  7. Pass-Ring — Dwarf road priority for one train of carts. `[TRAVEL]` `[AUTHORITY]`

    The ring is iron. Wear it on your off hand. The Aeler outcasts who made it stamped their names inside. One name is scratched out—the smith was killed in a feud. The ring still works. The ring has eight runes. The ninth is a scar.

    Blood-price: The ring can be used as a toll waiver for any dwarf road (value 2 Supply). Once used, the ring cracks.

  8. Bride-Escrow — Hold the bride-gift; both sides must humour you. `[SOCIAL]` `[WEIGHT]`

    The purse is a leather bag. The coins inside are from a dead man's hoard. The dead man was a Viterran lord who tried to tax the clans. His ghost asks for his money back. The purse has eight seams. The ninth is a stitch.

    Guest-right cost: The ghost will appear if the purse is opened without a witness. If you fail to provide a witness, start Haunted [4].

  9. Shelter Writ — Gray Tor opens its gates during storm or pursuit. `[SOCIAL]`

    The writ is a raven feather. Burn it to claim shelter. The raven was a clan spy. His memory still watches the gates. The feather has eight barbs. The ninth is a secret.

    Guest-right cost: The writ only works if you swear an oath of non-violence within the fort. Refusal voids the writ.

    J
    Oath-Bracelet — One binding vow ends cleanly, witnessed. `[OATH]` `[MAGIC]`

    The bracelet is silver. The clasp is a wolf's head. Bite it to break the oath. The wolf's head was a seal of a Viterran king. The oath was sworn under duress. The bracelet remembers. The bracelet has eight links. The ninth is the bite.

    Cairn vote: Breaking the oath triggers a cairn vote. The dead always vote for the wronged party—advance the related Feud timer by +1 per broken oath.

    Q
    Council Audience — The Cairns hear you alone; precedent sticks like stone. `[SOCIAL]` `[LAW]`

    The audience is held at midnight. The stones glow when they agree. The last audience exiled a clan chief. He is still walking the passes, looking for a cairn that will forgive him. There are eight councilors. The ninth is the stone.

    Guest-right cost: You must leave an offering of silence (no speaking for one hour) before the audience. If you break silence, the cairns refuse to judge.

    K
    Road Commission — Collect tolls on a stretch of pass (for now). `[AUTHORITY]` `[TRADE]`

    The commission is a wooden staff. Plant it at the toll gate. The staff was carved from a gallows tree. The last toll-keeper was hanged. The staff still creaks. The staff has eight knots. The ninth is a creak.

    Blood-price: The commission allows you to demand 1 Supply from any traveler. If you abuse it, the cairns vote against you—start Ancestral Grudge +1.

    A
    Stone-Clause — Temporary exception to dwarf toll or law, sealed. `[AUTHORITY]` `[OATH]`

    The clause is a single rune. Carve it on the toll post, and the mountain will honor it—once. The rune was taught to the clans by an Aeler outcast who wanted to see a Viterran knight pay double. The rune has eight strokes. The ninth is the mountain's answer.

    Guest-right cost: Using the clause obliges you to perform a service for the Aeler outcasts (a quest). Refusal starts Deep Road +1.
